reason: Machine lens: all opcodes are NMOS-era (LDA/STA abs,Y, LDA/STA abs, LDA zp), real on the 65SC12. abs,Y forms the same 16-bit effective address as (zp),Y (wrap at &FFFF), so rows past &7FFF behave identically; the load's page-cross +1 is the same condition; STA abs,Y is a flat 5 vs STA (zp),Y 6. Per byte 4+5+2=11 vs 5+6+2=13 (crossings equal), BPL/BMI unchanged; setup 4 x LDA zp (3) + 16 x STA abs (4) = 76. Bytes: setup 56 + loop 28 vs 20 = +64 (claim -64 = grows 64). Listing: old loop &30D9-&30EF in page &30; new sdw_l1 &3111, BPL at &312D, next &312F: no branch page cross. BNE part now 88 bytes forward, BPL 30 back, BMI next_row 66 (unchanged): all in range. line8 moves &3104->&3144, entries to &3167, HI(line8) still computed (cell+2 written), so the existing self-mod is intact. The new self-modified operands are written in the same instruction stream, same ACCCON X as execution, like cell+1; render_reset copies &3000-&3FFF main to shadow so both copies carry the code; nothing else references sky_draw.whole. sky_zero (&317E..) loops stay in page &31; per-screen vars and sky_img0 (&31BF..&337F) move, sky_blk_lo/hi built from the label, SKY_IMG_SIZE ends at &337F under &3400 (free SKIP shrinks 193->129; ASSERT at game.6502:5333 guards gameplay builds). Only the cycle claim is overstated: window counts give BMI next_row 4.4 cycles/pass = 1.47 whole rows/pass (not 1.1) and ~94.6 bytes/pass, so savings ~2*94.6-76*1.47 = ~78 cycles/pass, ~53 per execution (2*64 bytes - 76), image page-cross shifts aside; still a net gain, consistent with the measured -148 render cycles.
